rationale_overall: The week's pool was dominated by non-investable noise: Iran/Yemen/Israel missile and nuclear-tension geopolitical events with no tradable US ticker, Chinese state-run space (Shenzhou-20) and nuclear-plant announcements (Daya Bay, five new reactor approvals) with no US listing, private companies (SpaceX Starship/Falcon 9 launches, Xanadu quantum partnerships), foreign/OTC names (Huawei AI chip, Indian warship builder, DRDO Astra missile), and generic AI-education/AI-liability commentary pieces with no ticker attached. Two items had a real US-listed angle: Amazon's first Kuiper satellite deployment (AMZN) and Rocket Lab's HASTE launch contract award from Kratos Defense for the DOD (RKLB) — a genuine commercial win in the rockets & spacecraft wave. Neither rises to the bar for a swap this week: AMZN is a diversified mega-cap already highly correlated with the existing AAPL/GOOGL/MSFT/NVDA block, not a rising pure-play, and RKLB's single contract win, while a legitimate buildup signal worth tracking for a future rebalance, is not yet strong enough evidence of thesis breach in any current holding (AI wave is still intact, no negative catalysts surfaced for AAPL/GOOGL/MSFT/NVDA this week) to justify displacing a core AI position. Holding steady this week; RKLB remains on watch for a future period if wave-news volume builds.
